newsitem.title: USA: Group demands fair racial policy from Shell Oil.
newsitem.headline: Group demands fair racial policy from Shell Oil.

text.p: Activists and others involved in racial discrimination lawsuits against Shell Oil Co gathered Wednesday in a black neighborhood here to demand fair racial practices once the company combines its downstream refining and marketing operations with Texaco .

Shell faces two class-action lawsuits alleging it discriminates against black employees and Texaco recently paid $176.1 miilion to settle a suit by black workers who say they were denied raises and promotions on the basis of their race.
"We don't want Shell's policies to predominate in the merger. If they do we'll be back at square one," said Noah Griffin, a spokesman for the plaintiffs who are filing the lawsuits against Shell.
"There's still outstanding racial discrimination issues with Shell as there were with Texaco," Griffin said.
The merger will give Shell a 56 percent stake in the new company and 44 percent to Texaco.
The companies will gain a 14 percent share of the retail gasoline market in regions covered by the combined merger.
"People are concerned about who they buy their gas from," Griffin said.
